description: Getting past the model's fixed clip length by running one pipeline repeatedly and stitching the output. The default is a 'guide' chain: each segment's last `guide_frames` frames (22 or 39, default 22) and their audio are laid into the next at frame 0 as an H3 guide, the next keyframe is the guide's first frame, and the guide is trimmed off again, so motion and voice carry across the seam and 'trim_frames' and the crossfade do not apply (the run logs that). Guide is the default because the counter round measured it best for every shot type (bench/records/counters.md); guides are t2va/fl2va only, so the ref2va chains have no 'guide' mode. Set `continuity` to 'last_frame' for the uncommon case - no voice to carry, or a deliberate fresh-keyframe look: each segment's final frame becomes the next segment's keyframe, and then 'frame_snap' keeps every segment a length the model accepts, 'trim_frames' drops the duplicated keyframe at each seam, and a crossfade over the generated audio hides the joins. `prompt` is used for every segment, so a spoken line in it repeats in each one; pass `prompts`, one prompt per segment, to give each its own. To ask for a length instead of a count, set `duration_seconds`; it overrides `segments` (the run logs that `segments` was ignored), and the plan derives the segments and the video and audio are trimmed to exactly that length (not with a guide back-off or carry_pick). 'keep_segments' (default false) saves each segment as a playable mp4 beside the take and keeps it, naming it on the take's shots - what 'repair-segment' needs to re-render one segment in place later. 'shot' picks the drift counters measured for a kind of shot (bench/records/counters.md), through 'presets'; any variable you pass still wins. 'moving' (the default) is guide with no counters. 'static' (locked-off camera, subject in front) applies continuity 'guide' with anchor 'segment_1' at anchor_strength 0.25. 'dialogue' (a speaking subject in motion) is guide with no counters. 'static_long' (a static take past about 30 s) is guide with keystone 'segment_1' at keystone_slot 'last': segment 1's opening frame is every later segment's last image, which held the backdrop and the face for two minutes on two seeds where 'static' crusts from about 42 s; its price is the subject easing back to the opening pose at the end of each segment, about every 4.25 s, and about +9 min (+17%) wall on a two-minute take (bench/records/structural.md, *Keystone slot*). Pass `keystone_slot: first` for plain keystone (backdrop resets in a mid-shot pop) or `keystone: none` with `keystone_slot: null` for none; never use it on a moving shot. To turn the anchor off on a static shot, pass `anchor_strength: null` as well (the bundle's 0.25 survives and a strength with no anchor is refused), or use `shot: moving`. The cost row is the guide chain at 3 x 124 frames, 13.5 min (the seam A/B, C-F311, docs/proposals/complete/h3-guides-complete.md); last_frame measured 9.6. A static take longer than about 30 s is `shot: static_long`, measured to two minutes; on 'static' the drift builds past 30 s and the take should be cut into shots of 30 s or less. Never use 'last_frame' with 'look_hold' or 'carry_pick' on an H3 camera move: it froze the camera on an orbit (an LTX chain is not held back, so templates/ltx2/chained-segments holds the look by default). `tier` (default 'standard') moves canvas, steps and weights together through 'presets', measured on the long-form bench (bench/records/tiers.md); any variable you pass still wins. 'draft' is 4 steps on the standard canvas and weights, about 30% less wall time, and keeps the standard take's staging at the same seed, so approve blocking and timing on it, never texture. 'standard' is the template's own defaults (960x544, int4). 'best' is 1344x768, the turbo LoRA's own canvas, on int8 weights: the least crust measured, at about 1.7x standard's wall time; it re-stages, so it is a render of its own, not a final of the draft.
summary: A long H3 clip from a still, chained with guide continuity by default and shot-type presets.

vram_estimate.reason: each segment is one H3 run, so the ceiling is a segment's: the t2va calibration (#324) - peak activation memory scales with width * height * num_frames - plus, under 'guide' continuity, the guide each segment after the first is given, which is encoded on the target canvas and costs about as much per voxel as the clip itself (docs/proposals/h3-guide-vram.md, #694)

variables.prompt:
For the target video, at 0.00 seconds into the target video, <Picture 1> (from [Shot 1]) is fully referenced.

integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] Cinematic, live-action macro photography with a shallow depth of field, one continuous shot. The shot opens exactly on <Picture 1>: a translucent blown glass figure fills the frame against a dark, softly graded background, its surface catching cool rim light along every curve and throwing small caustics onto the surface beneath it. Its tentacles writhe without pause, curling and uncurling in slow deliberate coils, the glass flexing as though molten while staying perfectly clear. The figure (S1), a deep cavernous male voice with a long tail of reverb, unhurried and very low in pitch, speaks steadily throughout, <d>[English] Rise now. The old ones are listening.</d> Its central mass swells and contracts with the cadence of the words, and the caustics on the surface below ripple in time. The camera holds a static shot, letting the tentacles move through the frame edges.

overall_soundscape: A dark, near-silent room tone under a faint low-frequency hum. The tentacle movement carries a fine, dry glass-on-glass squeak and an occasional soft chime as two limbs touch, continuous and unhurried from the first frame to the last.

non_diegetic_music: A sustained low drone of bowed double bass and detuned synthesiser, almost subsonic, holding an even intensity with no discernible melody or pulse.

num_frames.reason: the video VAE encodes 17 * n + 5 frames, and MiniMax-H3 generates between 5 and 15 seconds at 24 fps

width.reason: MiniMax-H3's pipeline refuses a `width` or `height` that is not a multiple of 32, and only after the weights have loaded; refused here instead, with no 'snap', since rounding would be a silent change to the size asked for
